tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why does the man think it is difficult to make the decision?

options.A: They have to make a choice by the end of the day.
options.B: Both candidates are very keen on getting the job.
options.C: They hold different views on the procedure.
options.D: Both candidates are quite competitive.

questions.cn: 男士为什么觉得这个决定难做？

optionsCn.A: 他们必须今天之内做出选择。
optionsCn.B: 两位候选人都非常想得到这份工作。
optionsCn.C: 他们对流程持不同看法。
optionsCn.D: 两位候选人都很有竞争力。

questions.stem: What do the speakers say may be worth noting?

options.A: Both Rachel and Peter came across as respectful and professional.
options.B: Rachel scored moderately higher grades than Peter at school.
options.C: Both Rachel and Peter excelled in their academic pursuit.
options.D: Peter appeared slightly stronger than Rachel physically.

questions.cn: 两位说话人说哪一点可能值得记下？

optionsCn.A: 蕾切尔和彼得都给人恭敬、专业的印象。
optionsCn.B: 蕾切尔在校成绩比彼得略高一些。
optionsCn.C: 蕾切尔和彼得在学业上都很出色。
optionsCn.D: 彼得在身体上似乎比蕾切尔略强。

questions.stem: According to the man, what might account for Peter appearing somewhat more self-assured than Rachel?

options.B: His accumulation of experience.
options.C: His unusual state of mind.
options.D: His knowledge about the company.

questions.cn: 根据男士，什么可能解释彼得显得比蕾切尔更有自信？

optionsCn.C: 他不寻常的心态。
optionsCn.D: 他对公司的了解。

questions.stem: What does the man say they will do if they can’t reach an agreement?

options.A: Compare the candidates side by side again.
options.B: Ask the board to cast the deciding vote.
options.C: Find a way to break the tie next time.
options.D: Let John make the final decision.

questions.cn: 男士说如果两人无法达成一致，他们会怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 再次把两位候选人并排比较。
optionsCn.C: 下次找个办法打破平局。
optionsCn.D: 让约翰做最终决定。

lines.t: We are down to two candidates for one position, and we need to decide by the end of the day in order to finalize this whole procedure.
lines.cn: 这个职位只剩两位候选人了，我们今天之内必须定下来，好把整个流程走完。

lines.t: Yes, but it isn’t an easy choice to make.
lines.cn: 是啊，但这选择不好做。

lines.t: Both applicants are quite strong.
lines.cn: 两位申请人都相当优秀。

lines.t: Let’s get to it, then.
lines.cn: 那就开始吧。

lines.t: Both of them went to good universities, and both of them studied business-related subjects.
lines.cn: 两人都上过好大学，也都学的是商科相关专业。

lines.t: So academically, I’d say they’re pretty much the same.
lines.cn: 所以就学业而言，我觉得两人基本不相上下。

lines.t: What do you think?
lines.cn: 你觉得呢？

lines.t: I would agree, yes.
lines.cn: 我同意，是的。

lines.t: The only difference worth noting, perhaps, is that it looks like Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university.
lines.cn: 也许唯一值得一提的是，蕾切尔在高中和大学的成绩似乎都略高一些。

lines.t: But as I said, only a tiny bit higher than Peter.
lines.cn: 但正如我说的，只比彼得高一点点。

lines.t: That’s true, and worth noting.
lines.cn: 确实如此，值得记下。

lines.t: In addition, Rachel interviewed very well.
lines.cn: 此外，蕾切尔的面试表现很好。

lines.t: I thought she came across as bright and alert.
lines.cn: 我觉得她给人的印象是聪明机敏。

lines.t: Yes.
lines.cn: 是的。

lines.t: She asked some very good questions about the position and the company, which made me think she is very keen about the job.
lines.cn: 她问了一些关于职位和公司的很好的问题，让我觉得她对这份工作非常上心。

lines.t: I thought so, too.
lines.cn: 我也这么觉得。

lines.t: Now, let’s look at Peter’s interview performance.
lines.cn: 现在来看看彼得的面试表现。

lines.t: I thought he also did very well.
lines.cn: 我觉得他也表现得很好。

lines.t: He came across as respectful and professional, wouldn’t you say?
lines.cn: 他给人恭敬、专业的感觉，你不觉得吗？

lines.t: Calm and poised.
lines.cn: 沉着镇定。

lines.t: Very mature for his age.
lines.cn: 以他的年龄来说非常成熟。

lines.t: Exactly.
lines.cn: 正是。

lines.t: In my notes, I wrote that he seemed composed and in control of his emotions.
lines.cn: 我在笔记里写道，他显得沉着、情绪自控。

lines.t: I think he definitely looked more mature than Rachel.
lines.cn: 我觉得他明显比蕾切尔更成熟。

lines.t: Interesting.
lines.cn: 有意思。

lines.t: So, we agree that Rachel appeared inexperienced and less mature than Peter, even though both candidates are the same age and have practically no work experience.
lines.cn: 所以我们都认为蕾切尔显得缺乏经验、不如彼得成熟，尽管两人年龄相同、也几乎都没有工作经验。

lines.t: When comparing them side by side, yes, Peter seemed more self-assured somehow.
lines.cn: 把他们并排比较时，是的，彼得似乎更有自信。

lines.t: Maybe it was something about their body language.
lines.cn: 也许是他们的肢体语言给人的感觉。

lines.t: Sure. Maybe he was simply less nervous.
lines.cn: 当然。也许他只是没那么紧张。

lines.t: Maybe.
lines.cn: 也许吧。

lines.t: Who knows?
lines.cn: 谁知道呢？

lines.t: To be honest, I think I like Rachel better.
lines.cn: 说实话，我觉得我更喜欢蕾切尔。

lines.t: Hmm.
lines.cn: 嗯。

lines.t: Really?
lines.cn: 真的吗？

lines.t: I think I like Peter.
lines.cn: 我觉得我喜欢彼得。

lines.t: Ah, well.
lines.cn: 啊，好吧。

lines.t: If there’s a tie, and we can’t come to an agreement, then we’ll take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote.
lines.cn: 如果打平、我们又无法达成一致，那就交给约翰，由他投决定票。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What are the speakers mainly talking about?

options.B: The woman’s latest collection.
options.C: This season’s new fashion.
options.D: The head designer’s role.

questions.cn: 两位说话人主要在谈什么？

optionsCn.C: 这一季的新时尚。
optionsCn.D: 首席设计师的角色。

questions.stem: What does the woman say she always tries to incorporate into her aesthetic?

options.B: Something meeting public expectations.
options.C: Something slightly absurd.
options.D: Something a bit ambiguous.

questions.cn: 女士说她总想在审美中加入什么？

optionsCn.C: 略显荒诞的东西。
optionsCn.D: 有点模糊含混的东西。

questions.stem: What does the woman say she likes to do?

options.A: Merge styles often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum.
options.B: Learn from the designs of the Asian rural mountain villagers.
options.C: Make velvet capes look both majestic and masculine.
options.D: Draw intricate patterns onto a traditional power suit.

questions.cn: 女士说她喜欢做什么？

optionsCn.A: 融合常处于时尚光谱两端的风格。
optionsCn.B: 向亚洲山村民众的设计学习。
optionsCn.C: 让天鹅绒披风既恢宏又阳刚。
optionsCn.D: 在传统权力套装上画出繁复图案。

questions.stem: What is the man looking forward to?

options.B: Seeing the woman’s new creations.
options.C: Incorporating indigenous aspects into his work.
options.D: Sharing more ideas with the woman next time.

questions.cn: 男士期待什么？

optionsCn.C: 把本土元素融入他的作品。
optionsCn.D: 下次和女士分享更多想法。

lines.t: We’re here with Clementine Ortega, head designer of the private fashion label L’Orange, to discuss her latest collection.
lines.cn: 今天我们请到了私人时装品牌 L'Orange 的首席设计师克莱门汀·奥尔特加，来谈谈她的最新系列。

lines.t: Ms. Ortega, how would you describe this season’s look?
lines.cn: 奥尔特加女士，您会如何描述这一季的造型？

lines.t: To be honest, my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side, and I think this collection is even more so.
lines.cn: 说实话，我一向偏爱偏模糊含混的风格，我觉得这个系列更是如此。

lines.t: I try not to adhere to social norms and expectations.
lines.cn: 我尽量不遵循社会规范和期待。

lines.t: Rather, I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd into my aesthetic.
lines.cn: 相反，我总是试着在审美中融入一些略显荒诞的东西。

lines.t: The assortments of accessories in this collection have had quite the impact on critics.
lines.cn: 这个系列中搭配的各式配饰对评论界影响不小。

lines.t: The dazzling cape deployed at the end of the show, for example, bewildered many in the audience.
lines.cn: 比如大秀结尾那件耀眼的披风，让在场许多观众都看呆了。

lines.t: What was your inspiration for this piece?
lines.cn: 这件作品的灵感来自哪里？

lines.t: Over the summer, I traveled through rural mountain villages throughout Asia in search of handicrafts to decorate my new studio with.
lines.cn: 整个夏天，我在亚洲各地穿行于山乡村落，寻找手工艺品来装饰我的新工作室。

lines.t: The embroidery done by the women in a particular village was so exquisite.
lines.cn: 某个村子里妇女们的刺绣精美极了。

lines.t: I couldn’t stop thinking about it.
lines.cn: 我一直对它念念不忘。

lines.t: Trying to recreate their designs would have been futile.
lines.cn: 想复刻她们的设计是徒劳的。

lines.t: So instead, I applied my own eccentric approach.
lines.cn: 于是我改用了自己的怪诞手法。

lines.t: Using glitter, I drew similar intricate patterns onto the velvet cape.
lines.cn: 我用闪粉在天鹅绒披风上画出类似的繁复图案。

lines.t: This ended up in the glamorous, luminous look that concluded the show.
lines.cn: 最终成就了那件为整场秀收尾的华丽、流光的作品。

lines.t: It was indeed majestic, and yet, dare I say, masculine at the same time.
lines.cn: 它确实气势恢宏，而且，我敢说，同时又带着阳刚之气。

lines.t: Well, yes, that was intentional.
lines.cn: 嗯，是的，那是刻意为之的。

lines.t: I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum.
lines.cn: 我喜欢把通常处于时尚光谱两端的风格融合起来。

lines.t: Hence, the sparkling cape was paired with a traditional power suit you would typically see in a business setting.
lines.cn: 因此，那件闪亮披风搭配了一套商务场合常见的传统权力套装。

lines.t: It was sensational, if I do say so myself.
lines.cn: 恕我自夸，那真是轰动全场。

lines.t: Spectacular for sure!
lines.cn: 绝对称得上壮观！

lines.t: A stunning show all around.
lines.cn: 整场秀都令人惊艳。

lines.t: Going against stereotypes, the incorporation of indigenous aspects, along with your underlying signature touch, made this collection a statement of the season.
lines.cn: 打破刻板印象，把本土元素融入其中，再加上您标志性的个人笔触，让这个系列成为本季的宣言。

lines.t: You have proven yourself a formidable young designer, and we can’t wait to see what creations you come up with next.
lines.cn: 您已证明自己是位了不起的年轻设计师，我们迫不及待想看您接下来会有什么新作。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about 80% of participating dogs in the new study?

options.A: They could readily recognize their owner simply by looking.
options.B: They could understand the implications of human commands.
options.C: They could be domesticated to act as our companions.
options.D: They could follow pointing gestures without training.

questions.cn: 文章说新研究中 80% 的参与犬如何？

optionsCn.A: 它们只要看一眼就能认出主人。
optionsCn.B: 它们能理解人类指令的含义。
optionsCn.C: 它们可以被驯化来给我们做伴。
optionsCn.D: 它们未经训练就能跟随指向手势。

questions.stem: What may help alleviate the problem caused by stray dogs?

options.A: Cultivating them to be intelligent creatures.
options.B: Training them to behave like domesticated dogs.
options.C: Understanding how humans impact their behavior.
options.D: Taking measures to reduce their numbers.

questions.cn: 什么可能有助于缓解流浪狗造成的问题？

optionsCn.A: 把它们培养成聪明的生物。
optionsCn.B: 训练它们像家犬一样行事。
optionsCn.C: 理解人类如何影响它们的行为。
optionsCn.D: 采取措施减少它们的数量。

questions.stem: What do the researchers suggest we do to reduce conflicts between stray dogs and humans?

options.B: Treat them with sensitivity and respect.
options.C: Make them responsive to our commands.
options.D: Watch their behavior and try to improve it.

questions.cn: 研究者建议我们怎么做以减少流浪狗与人之间的冲突？

optionsCn.A: 通过反复训练驯服它们。
optionsCn.B: 以体恤和尊重的方式对待它们。
optionsCn.C: 让它们对我们的指令有反应。
optionsCn.D: 观察它们的行为并设法改进。

lines.t: Pet dogs can often readily understand a wide range of their owners’ commands and gestures, but are these abilities inborn or are they exclusively learned through training?
lines.cn: 宠物狗往往能轻松理解主人各种各样的指令和手势，但这些能力是天生的，还是只能通过训练习得？

lines.t: To find out, a new study examined whether stray dogs could understand human gestures.
lines.cn: 为了弄清这一点，一项新研究考察了流浪狗是否能理解人类手势。

lines.t: The study revealed that 80% of participating dogs successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location despite having never received prior training.
lines.cn: 研究显示，参与实验的狗中有 80% 成功跟随指向某个具体位置的手势，尽管它们此前从未接受过训练。

lines.t: The results suggest that dogs can understand complex gestures by simply watching humans.
lines.cn: 结果表明，狗只要观察人类，就能理解复杂的手势。

lines.t: This could have implications in reducing conflict between stray dogs and humans.
lines.cn: 这可能有助于减少流浪狗与人之间的冲突。

lines.t: Dogs were domesticated 10,000 to 15,000 years ago.
lines.cn: 狗在 1 万至 1.5 万年前被驯化。

lines.t: This means they are probably the oldest domesticated animals on the planet.
lines.cn: 这意味着它们大概是地球上最早的被驯化动物。

lines.t: Humans then bred dogs with the most desirable and useful traits so that they could function as companions and workers.
lines.cn: 随后人类把最具理想、最有用特质的狗繁育下来，让它们既能做伴又能干活。

lines.t: This resulted in domesticated dogs that are highly responsive to human commands and gestures.
lines.cn: 由此得到的家犬对人类指令和手势的响应度极高。

lines.t: However, it was not clear whether dogs understand us through training alone, or whether this was an inherent ability.
lines.cn: 然而，狗究竟只是通过训练才理解我们，还是这本身就是一种固有能力，此前并不清楚。

lines.t: Why does this matter?
lines.cn: 这为什么重要？

lines.t: Stray dogs are a common feature in cities around the world.
lines.cn: 流浪狗是世界各地城市的常见景象。

lines.t: They may observe and occasionally interact with people, but such dogs have never been trained, and are behaviorally “wild”.
lines.cn: 它们可能观察人类、偶尔与之互动，但这类狗从未受过训练，行为上是“野”的。

lines.t: Conflicts between stray dogs and humans are a problem.
lines.cn: 流浪狗与人之间的冲突是个问题。

lines.t: Understanding how humans shape stray dogs’ behavior may help alleviate this problem.
lines.cn: 理解人类如何塑造流浪狗的行为，可能有助于缓解这个问题。

lines.t: According to the researchers of the new study, stray dogs are intelligent creatures.
lines.cn: 据这项新研究的研究者说，流浪狗是聪明的生物。

lines.t: They closely observe humans and use their understanding of us to make a decision.
lines.cn: 它们密切观察人类，并利用对人类的了解来做决定。

lines.t: Treating stray dogs with sensitivity and respect, and giving them space, the researchers assert, can reduce much conflict.
lines.cn: 研究者断言，以体恤和尊重的方式对待流浪狗、给它们空间，能减少许多冲突。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why is food product placement within the fridge very important?

options.A: The temperature inside it varies from place to place.
options.B: Proper placement facilitates access to food products.
options.C: Its different shelves are designed for different purposes.
options.D: The space in an average fridge changes from top to bottom.

questions.cn: 为什么食物在冰箱里的摆放位置很重要？

optionsCn.A: 冰箱内部各处温度不同。
optionsCn.B: 合理摆放便于取用食品。
optionsCn.C: 不同的层架各有设计用途。
optionsCn.D: 普通冰箱的空间从上到下都在变化。

questions.stem: What does the passage say is the whole purpose of the modern refrigerator?

options.A: To slow the rising of temperature in it.
options.B: To provide a big box of evenly cold air.
options.C: To prevent germs from growing quickly.
options.D: To keep the food cold as long as possible.

questions.cn: 文章说现代冰箱存在的全部意义是什么？

optionsCn.B: 提供一大箱均匀的冷空气。
optionsCn.C: 防止细菌快速繁殖。
optionsCn.D: 让食物尽可能长时间保持低温。

questions.stem: Where in the fridge should we store foods already cooked?

options.B: In the middle section.
options.C: On the inside of its doors.
options.D: At the back of its bottom shelf.

questions.cn: 已做熟的食物应放在冰箱哪里？

optionsCn.C: 在门内侧。
optionsCn.D: 在下层最里面。

questions.stem: Why should we never store foods with high water content at the back of the bottom shelf?

options.B: They will be hard to defrost.
options.C: They will be contaminated.
options.D: They will be ruined.

questions.cn: 为什么绝不能把含水量高的食物放在下层最里面？

optionsCn.C: 它们会被污染。
optionsCn.D: 它们会被毁掉。

lines.t: Think your refrigerator is just one big box of evenly cold air?
lines.cn: 你以为冰箱就是一个装满均匀冷空气的大箱子？

lines.t: Not so!
lines.cn: 并非如此！

lines.t: The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top and everywhere in between.
lines.cn: 普通冰箱内部的温度其实从前到后、从下到上、以及各处之间都在变化。

lines.t: Because of this, food product placement within the appliance is far more important than you probably realize.
lines.cn: 正因如此，食物在冰箱里的摆放位置远比你意识到的更重要。

lines.t: The whole purpose of the modern refrigerator is to slow the growth of bacteria, which thrive in temperatures from 4.4 to 60 degrees Celsius.
lines.cn: 现代冰箱存在的全部意义就是减缓细菌繁殖，而细菌在 4.4 至 60 摄氏度之间最为活跃。

lines.t: As a result, refrigerators are typically set at or below that low end to protect foods against bacteria.
lines.cn: 因此，冰箱通常设定在该温度区间的下限或更低，以防食物受细菌侵害。

lines.t: Although it might seem like time spent organizing the fridge will spoil your day, doing so will actually make it more user-friendly, easier to clean and food safety-conscious.
lines.cn: 虽然花时间整理冰箱看起来像在耽误时间，但这样做实际上会让它更好用、更易清洁，也更利于食品安全。

lines.t: Those little bins on the inside of refrigerator doors are convenient, but they don’t maintain a consistent temperature, so definitely refrain from putting perishable foods in there.
lines.cn: 冰箱门内侧的那些小格子很方便，但它们无法保持恒温，所以千万别把易腐食物放在那里。

lines.t: The top area is not as cold as the bottom of the fridge, so save it for the foods that don’t need extra-chilly temperatures.
lines.cn: 上层区域不如冰箱底部冷，所以留给那些不需要特别低温的食物。

lines.t: Store foods that are ready to eat or already cooked on the top shelf.
lines.cn: 即食或已做熟的食物放在最上层。

lines.t: The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge, so place eggs here.
lines.cn: 中层是冰箱里温度控制最好的一部分，所以把鸡蛋放在这里。

lines.t: Drinks and prepared foods can also live on the middle shelf if you ran out of room up top.
lines.cn: 如果上层放不下了，饮料和备好的食物也可以放在中层。

lines.t: The back of the bottom shelf is the coldest spot in the fridge, so store perishable dairy products here to keep them edible longer.
lines.cn: 下层最里面是冰箱里最冷的位置，所以把易腐的乳制品放在这里，能保存更久。

lines.t: Never store foods with high water content here, because the water within them can and will freeze, effectively ruining them.
lines.cn: 千万不要把含水量高的食物放在这里，因为它们内部的水会结冰，把食物彻底毁掉。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say is quite common among older people?

options.B: Growing feebleness.
options.C: Hip fracture.
options.D: Fatal infections.

questions.cn: 讲话者说什么是老年人中相当常见的情况？

optionsCn.C: 髋部骨折。
optionsCn.D: 致命感染。

questions.stem: What does the speaker think excites her most about her research?

options.B: It contributes to psychology.
options.C: It outcompetes lots of academics’ research.
options.D: It wins recognition outside of Birmingham.

questions.cn: 讲话者认为她的研究最让她兴奋的是什么？

optionsCn.C: 它胜过许多学者的研究。
optionsCn.D: 它赢得伯明翰之外的认可。

questions.stem: How does the speaker approach her research project?

options.A: By bringing together experts old and young.
options.B: By counting on advanced modern technology.
options.C: By making full use of her expertise.
options.D: By combining multiple perspectives.

questions.cn: 讲话者如何进行她的研究项目？

optionsCn.A: 汇聚老一代和年轻一代的专家。
optionsCn.C: 充分发挥她自己的专长。
optionsCn.D: 结合多种视角。

lines.t: My current research is mainly looking at factors like stress and how it affects our immune system.
lines.cn: 我目前的研究主要关注压力等因素及其对免疫系统的影响。

lines.t: So the current projects that I’m quite excited about are looking at older people and factors that are important to them.
lines.cn: 眼下让我非常兴奋的项目，研究对象是老年人以及对他们重要的因素。

lines.t: In one project we are looking at hip fracture in older people, which is a common event and we’re trying to understand the impact of depression.
lines.cn: 其中一个项目研究老年人髋部骨折——这是很常见的情况——我们试图了解抑郁所起的作用。

lines.t: Often people in hospital with a hip fracture develop depression, and these are the people that then go on to become feeble a lot more quickly than others.
lines.cn: 髋部骨折住院的人常常出现抑郁，而这些人随后会比其他人更快变得虚弱。

lines.t: They get infections.
lines.cn: 他们会发生感染。

lines.t: Often these infections lead to death.
lines.cn: 这些感染常常导致死亡。

lines.t: So we’re trying to slow down that progression to feebleness.
lines.cn: 所以我们在努力延缓这种走向衰弱的过程。

lines.t: So if we can better understand how these factors interact, then we can actually start doing something about it.
lines.cn: 如果我们能更好地理解这些因素如何相互作用，就能真正开始采取措施。

lines.t: The impact that my research will have in Birmingham, first of all, is obviously for older people because these are the people that are having hip fractures and developing depression, and we’re trying to improve their health and their quality of life.
lines.cn: 我的研究在伯明翰的影响，首先显而易见是惠及老年人，因为正是他们发生髋部骨折、出现抑郁，而我们努力改善他们的健康和生活质量。

lines.t: But this isn’t just a problem in Birmingham or even in the UK.
lines.cn: 但这不只是伯明翰的问题，甚至不只是英国的问题。

lines.t: This is a problem globally.
lines.cn: 这是个全球性问题。

lines.t: People are aging.
lines.cn: 人在变老。

lines.t: There’s a lot more people in the older generation who are living for longer but not necessarily staying healthy for a large part of their lives.
lines.cn: 老一代中寿命更长的人多了很多，但他们未必在人生的大部分时间里保持健康。

lines.t: So the last part of their life can often be full of ill health, and we’re trying to understand factors that can contribute to the quality of life later on.
lines.cn: 所以生命的最后阶段常常充满病痛，而我们正试图理解有哪些因素能影响晚年的生活质量。

lines.t: I think the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant.
lines.cn: 我觉得我的研究最让我兴奋的地方是，它真实而且切题。

lines.t: Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant to those around them.
lines.cn: 许多学者的研究大概也让他们十分兴奋，但未必与身边人有什么关联。

lines.t: Whereas I feel that the work I do is relevant to everyone because everyone is aging.
lines.cn: 而我觉得我做的事和每个人都相关，因为每个人都在变老。

lines.t: Health is an issue for everyone, regardless of their age, and what I’m trying to do is understand the factors that affect health and how we can improve the quality of life in people.
lines.cn: 健康是每个人的事，不分年龄，而我要做的是理解影响健康的因素，以及我们如何改善人们的生活质量。

lines.t: So that’s one of the things that really excites me about it.
lines.cn: 这是最让我兴奋的一点。

lines.t: One of the other things is, rather than just taking one perspective, so rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist, we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints to actually look at the sort of different factors affecting health.
lines.cn: 另一点是，我们不是只取一个视角——不再只从心理学家的角度看衰老与健康，而是把许多不同的技术和视角汇聚起来，去考察影响健康的各种因素。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about most colleges and graduate schools in America?

options.B: They don’t focus on teaching techniques.
options.C: They attach little importance to recipes.
options.D: They hire very few distinguished chefs.

questions.cn: 关于美国大多数大学和研究生院，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们不教基本的条理化方法。
optionsCn.C: 它们不重视菜谱。
optionsCn.D: 它们很少聘请杰出的厨师。

questions.stem: How do students of the culinary institute of America view “mise-en-place” or “put in place”?

options.B: It’s a way of transformation.
options.C: It’s too demanding for them.
options.D: It’s a way of life to them.

questions.cn: 美国烹饪学院的学生如何看待 mise-en-place（各就各位）？

optionsCn.C: 对他们来说要求太高。
optionsCn.D: 对他们来说是一种生活方式。

questions.stem: What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk?

options.A: Respect others so as to be respected.
options.B: Use time and resources in a wise way.
options.C: Cultivate a habit of self-discipline.
options.D: Learn from philosophers earnestly.

questions.cn: 讲话者在最后建议我们怎么做？

optionsCn.B: 明智地利用时间和资源。
optionsCn.C: 培养自律的习惯。
optionsCn.D: 认真向哲学家学习。

lines.t: Americans are obsessed with celebrity chefs.
lines.cn: 美国人对明星厨师的痴迷到了极点。

lines.t: We talk about them and try to eat like them.
lines.cn: 我们谈论他们，模仿他们的吃法。

lines.t: But could we learn something more from them than recipes and techniques?
lines.cn: 但除了菜谱和技法，我们还能从他们身上学到更多吗？

lines.t: According to market data enterprises, Americans spend nearly 10 billion dollars a year on self-help and personal organization products.
lines.cn: 据市场数据公司统计，美国人在自助和个人组织类产品上每年花费近 100 亿美元。

lines.t: The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don’t teach basic organization, but cooking schools and professional kitchens do.
lines.cn: 这个市场之所以巨大，部分原因是大多数大学和研究生院不教基本的条理化方法，而烹饪学校和专业厨房却会教。

lines.t: Perhaps the principles of cooking organization can be extended to help even those of us who aren’t top chefs.
lines.cn: 也许烹饪中的条理化原则可以推广开来，帮到我们这些并非顶级厨师的人。

lines.t: The system that makes kitchens function is called “mise-en-place”, or literally “put in place”.
lines.cn: 让厨房高效运转的这套方法叫“mise-en-place”，字面意思就是“各就各位”。

lines.t: It’s a French phrase that means to gather and arrange the ingredients and tools needed for cooking.
lines.cn: 这是个法语短语，意为把烹饪所需的食材和工具收集、摆好。

lines.t: But for many professional cooks, the phrase means something deeper.
lines.cn: 但对许多专业厨师来说，这个词的含义更深。

lines.t: Some cooks call it their religion.
lines.cn: 有些厨师称之为他们的信仰。

lines.t: It helps them coordinate vast amounts of labor and material, and transforms the lives of its practitioners through focus and self-discipline.
lines.cn: 它帮助他们协调大量的劳动力和物料，并通过专注与自律改变着践行者的生活。

lines.t: Students at the culinary institute of America view it as a way of life.
lines.cn: 美国烹饪学院的学生把它看作一种生活方式。

lines.t: It’s a way of concentrating their mind to only focus on the aspects that they need to be working on at the moment, to kind of rid themselves of distractions.
lines.cn: 它是一种让心思集中、只专注于当下该做之事、从而摆脱干扰的方式。

lines.t: And it’s a habit that some students carry with them even when they’re not in the kitchen.
lines.cn: 而且有些学生即使不在厨房里也保持这一习惯。

lines.t: They mise-en-place their life.
lines.cn: 他们把生活“各就各位”。

lines.t: They set up their books for class.
lines.cn: 把上课用的书摆好。

lines.t: They set up their chef whites.
lines.cn: 把厨师服摆好。

lines.t: They shine their shoes.
lines.cn: 把鞋擦亮。

lines.t: They know everything that they need every step of the day.
lines.cn: 一天中的每一步需要什么，他们都一清二楚。

lines.t: Then how does one attain this level of organization?
lines.cn: 那么，一个人如何达到这种条理化程度？

lines.t: The key to high-level organization is the mindset.
lines.cn: 高水平条理化的关键在于思维方式。

lines.t: Cooks can easily do six hours of preparation for a three-hour dinner shift.
lines.cn: 厨师可以轻松为三小时的晚餐时段做六小时的准备工作。

lines.t: “Mise-en-place forces cooks to account for every minute of their time and every movement.
lines.cn: “mise-en-place 迫使厨师把每一分钟、每一个动作都考虑在内。

lines.t: Every component of one single dish is in one single corner, so their hand literally moves inches.”,
lines.cn: 一道菜的每个组成部分都在一个角落里，所以他们的手移动的距离不过几英寸。”

lines.t: explains Dwayne Lipuma, an instructor at the culinary institute of America.
lines.cn: 美国烹饪学院教师德韦恩·利普马解释道。

lines.t: “Once students set up their station, I should be able to cover up their eyes.
lines.cn: “学生摆好工作台之后，我应该能把他们的眼睛蒙上。

lines.t: And they should know that their knives are always here, their oil is always right here, their salt and pepper is always right here.”
lines.cn: 他们也该知道，刀永远在这儿，油永远就在这儿，盐和胡椒永远就在这儿。”

lines.t: But practiced at its highest level, mise-en-place says that time is precious, resources are precious, space is precious, your self-respect and the respect of others are precious.
lines.cn: 但把 mise-en-place 践行到最高境界，它说的是：时间宝贵、资源宝贵、空间宝贵，你的自尊和别人的尊重都宝贵。

lines.t: Use them wisely.
lines.cn: 要善加利用。

lines.t: Isn’t that a philosophy for our time?
lines.cn: 这难道不正是为我们这个时代准备的哲学吗？

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What should self-acceptance be used as according to the speaker?

options.B: The reason for stagnation.
options.C: The basis for self-improvement.
options.D: The justification for self-confidence.

questions.cn: 根据讲话者，自我接纳应当被当作什么来用？

optionsCn.C: 自我提升的基础。
optionsCn.D: 自信的正当理由。

questions.stem: What do people tend to do when they have reached midlife?

options.B: Believe they have achieved their life goals.
options.C: Use a key tool for setting ambitious goals.
options.D: Stop imagining further progress in life.

questions.cn: 人到中年时往往会怎样？

optionsCn.B: 相信自己实现了人生目标。
optionsCn.C: 运用设定宏大目标的关键工具。
optionsCn.D: 不再想象人生中进一步的进步。

questions.stem: Why do we find ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal?

options.A: We feel we are always falling behind others.
options.B: We have to adapt to the ever-changing goal.
options.C: There are various misconceptions about goal setting.
options.D: There are always problems with the goal originally set.

questions.cn: 我们为什么因未达成目标而烦躁？

optionsCn.A: 我们觉得自己总落在别人后面。
optionsCn.B: 我们必须适应不断变化的目标。
optionsCn.C: 对设定目标存在各种误解。
optionsCn.D: 最初设定的目标总有问题。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say has an immediate positive impact on our thinking?

options.A: A noticeable change in the number of goals to achieve.
options.B: Measuring always against the gap rather than the gain.
options.C: Measuring where we’ve come from instead of measuring against the goal.
options.D: A proper conception of what we fail to notice in trying to achieve our goals.

questions.cn: 讲话者说什么对我们的思维有立即的积极影响？

optionsCn.A: 待实现目标数量的明显变化。
optionsCn.B: 总是拿差距而不是所得来衡量。
optionsCn.C: 衡量我们走过多远，而不是拿目标来衡量。
optionsCn.D: 对我们在追求目标时忽略了什么有正确的认识。

lines.t: Why do we stop making goals for ourselves and stop progressing in life?
lines.cn: 我们为什么不再给自己定目标，也不在人生中继续进步了？

lines.t: One reason is the belief that we should accept who we are and not constantly strive to improve ourselves.
lines.cn: 原因之一是这种信念：我们应当接受自己本来的样子，不该不断追求自我提升。

lines.t: The mistake we make with this is that whilst self-acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth.
lines.cn: 我们在此犯的错误是：自我接纳固然必要，但它其实应当被当作成长的基础。

lines.t: When we’re not growing, learning and seeking improvements in our lives, we tend to stagnate, accepting what is, and stop believing we can be better.
lines.cn: 当我们不再成长、学习、寻求生活中的改进时，我们就容易停滞，接受现状，不再相信自己能变得更好。

lines.t: A key tool for creating goals and progressing, is using our imagination.
lines.cn: 设定目标、取得进步的一个关键工具，就是运用我们的想象力。

lines.t: Yet as is so often the case, by the time we’ve reached midlife, we’ve stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve and feel quite negatively about goal setting.
lines.cn: 然而情况往往如此：到了中年，我们就不再梦想自己想要的成就，对设定目标也颇为消极。

lines.t: Instead of feeling confidence, happiness and satisfaction from achieving our goals, we feel we are always falling short.
lines.cn: 我们不再因实现目标而感到自信、快乐和满足，反而觉得自己总是差得远。

lines.t: That leads to disappointment, and we stop dreaming.
lines.cn: 这带来失望，于是我们不再做梦。

lines.t: We stop imagining the life we’d like to have or the person we’d like to be, quickly finding ourselves shattered by the pain of our reality.
lines.cn: 我们不再想象想要的生活、想成为的人，很快就发现自己被现实的痛苦击碎。

lines.t: Up until now, unless we work in the creative industry, we’ve found the idea of using “play” a bit childish.
lines.cn: 到目前为止，除非从事创意行业，我们总觉得“玩”这个念头有点幼稚。

lines.t: In the West, we’re mostly operating from our heads, the rational mind.
lines.cn: 在西方，我们大多靠头脑、靠理性思维运作。

lines.t: But it’s beginning to be better understood, because using our imagination is actually one of the most powerful things we could ever do.
lines.cn: 但这一点正逐渐被更好理解，因为运用想象力其实是我们能做的最强大的事情之一。

lines.t: The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes and we’re always adapting, whether we realize it or not.
lines.cn: 因未达成目标而烦躁，问题在于目标总在变化，而我们始终在适应，无论是否意识到。

lines.t: What happens, therefore, is that we end up feeling like we’re never going to reach our goals.
lines.cn: 于是结果就是，我们最终觉得自己永远达不到目标。

lines.t: And herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions and reasons for failure, dissatisfaction and unhappiness.
lines.cn: 这里就藏着最大的误解之一，也是失败、不满与不快乐的根源。

lines.t: We measure against the goal, rather than where we’ve come from.
lines.cn: 我们以目标为尺度衡量自己，而不是以自己走过多远来衡量。

lines.t: Dan Sullivan calls this “the gap and the gain”.
lines.cn: 丹·沙利文把这叫“差距与所得”。

lines.t: We measure always against the goal, which we never feel we’re reaching, rather than the gain, that is where we’ve come from.
lines.cn: 我们总是拿目标来衡量——那目标我们从不觉得自己能达到——而不是拿所得，也就是我们走过的路来衡量。

lines.t: In measuring where we’ve come from, rather than where we’re trying to get to, we see results.
lines.cn: 衡量自己走过多远，而不是要去的地方，我们就能看到成果。

lines.t: We see things we’ve taken for granted, or not noticed.
lines.cn: 我们看到那些被视作理所当然、或从未留意的东西。

lines.t: It’s a simple, yet profound change in perception, and what I love about it is the power it has to instantly shift us up a gear.
lines.cn: 这是认知上一次简单却深刻的转变，我喜欢它，是因为它能让我们的状态瞬间升一档。

lines.t: It’s so, so simple, yet has an immediate, positive impact on our thinking.
lines.cn: 它如此简单，却对我们的思维有立即而积极的影响。
